purpose: Teach: いくらか/わがまま/たびたび/めざす/ほめ/動揺/ぞう/当たら

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 孫のタカシ、たびたびわがまま言うらしいな。
lines.en: Our grandson Takashi, apparently he says selfish things quite often.
lines.style: Gentle observation, no judgment. Low, even tone. Pauses slightly as if remembering a recent moment. The cadence of someone comfortable with silence.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 子供だものね。学校でも一番をめざす真っ直ぐな子だわ。
lines.en: Well, he's only a child. He's such a straightforward boy—always aiming for first at school too.
lines.style: Warm defense wrapped in acceptance. Slight smile audible in the voice. Gentle emphasis on 「真っ直ぐな」—tender about his earnestness, not mocking it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 先日、先生にほめられたって電話あった。動揺するくらい嬉しかったよ。
lines.en: The other day there was a phone call—he'd gotten praise from his teacher. I was genuinely moved.
lines.style: Softness breaking into quiet emotion. Slight catch on the realization. Warm, almost vulnerable—the surprise of joy catching him off guard. Breath settles back into composure.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: ぞうさんの絵を描いて、コンクールで賞も当たったとか。
lines.en: He drew an elephant and won a prize in a contest, apparently.
lines.style: Bright, almost conspiratorial—sharing good news she's been holding. Light pace, warmth in the consonants. The sound of someone delighting in a grandchild's achievement.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 当たらないだろうと思ってたのに、いくらか自信もついたって。
lines.en: I never thought he'd win, but apparently it gave him a real boost of confidence.
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost marveling. Soft emphasis on 「当たらないだろう」—the surprise still there. Settles into quiet satisfaction. Steady, grounded warmth.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 今度遊びに来た時、たっぷり褒めましょう。
lines.en: Next time he comes to visit, we'll give him plenty of praise.
lines.style: Practical warmth with quiet determination. 「褒めましょう」lands with gentle conviction—a plan being set. The tenderness of an elder preparing generosity.
